title: NIST Next-Generation Wireless Testbed and O-RAN Standards Artifacts — Phase 65 Discovery technologies review
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Discovery technologies reporting pack. NIST's ongoing project page records open-source O-RAN testbed automation software, laboratory work using a 5G Open Testbed, and multiple 2025 contributions accepted into O-RAN test and security specifications supporting 5G/6G research.
key_findings: The project targets emerging security standards and guidance for 5G/6G Open RAN and core technologies.
NIST lists an open-source automation tool for deploying 5G O-RAN testbeds and an active 5G Open Testbed.
The page identifies multiple 2025 change requests accepted or incorporated into O-RAN test and security specification artifacts.
why_it_matters: Which records show a discovery instrument, dataset, testbed, or program becoming an inspectable research capability without treating availability as downstream use? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. This is an implementation record for test infrastructure and standards contributions, not merely a 6G policy aspiration.
ftfn_relevance: Adds concrete software, laboratory, change-request, and incorporated-specification artifacts to the 6G lane.
Defines later evidence gates for test results, certification, interoperability, 3GPP standards, and deployment.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
The artifacts support next-generation wireless research but do not constitute a completed 6G standard or commercial 6G network.
Accepted contributions do not prove broad interoperability, secure multi-vendor operation, certification, or federal deployment.
